A 17-year-old female presents to the emergency department with worsening abdominal and pelvic pain
that began 3 days ago. She describes the pain as diffuse, involving her abdomen, pelvis, and vagina.
She also reports vaginal itching and discharge. She works at an ice cream parlor and is sexually active
with multiple partners. Her vital signs are: temperature 97.6°F (36.7°C), blood pressure 110/71 mmHg,
pulse 69/min, respirations 17/min, and oxygen saturation 98% on room air. Physical examination
reveals diffuse abdominal tenderness, a foul-smelling thin white vaginal discharge, and the patient
scratching her vaginal area during the exam. What is the most appropriate first step in management?
Answer Choices: (A) KOH prep (B) Urinalysis (C) Nucleic acid amplification test (D) Urine hCG (E)
Vaginal pH testing (F) Pelvic ultrasound (G) Cervical swab and culture (H) Complete blood count (I)
Serum β-hCG (J) Wet mount
 A. Nucleic acid amplification test
B. Vaginal pH testing
C. Serum β-hCG
D. Pelvic ultrasound
E. Cervical swab and culture
F. Complete blood count
G. Wet mount
H. KOH prep
I. Urine hCG
J. Urinalysis
